extracted.intended_audience: theatre practitioners, teachers, educators, and students of improvisation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exercises for training actors in improvisation, organized into thematic sections (Status, Spontaneity, Narrative Skills, Masks and Trance) and intended for use in classrooms, rehearsal halls, and workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four main sections of the book ('Status').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a thematic area of work for a group to approach; the section contains specific techniques and exercises relating to status relationships and dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneity
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four main sections of the book ('Spontaneity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on fostering spontaneous responses and creativity in actors through exercises and techniques developed by Johnstone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Skills
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four main sections of the book ('Narrative Skills').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to develop actors' abilities to create and sustain narrative; these skills were developed further in actors' studio work and in demonstrations to schools and colleges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masks and Trance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four main sections of the book ('Masks and Trance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses work with masks and altered states as tools for improvisation and performance; presented as part of the sequence of areas a group might work through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific techniques and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: The book 'sets out the specific techniques and exercises which Johnstone has himself found most useful and most stimulating.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied criterion for producing effective improvisation training: rely on concrete, practiced exercises proven useful by an experienced practitioner; the book functions as an 'ideas book' of such exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Material is 'arranged more or less in the order a group might approach them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied guidance that exercises and topics should be sequenced appropriately for group learning—starting with foundational areas (e.g., Status, Spontaneity) before more advanced work (e.g., Masks and Trance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberating the imagination / cultivating creative power
rubrics_metrics.description: Stated pedagogical goal from critics: to 'liberate the imagination, to cultivate in the adult the creative power of the child.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative standard for improvisation work: exercises and teaching should encourage freedom, playfulness, and the recovery of a child's creative spontaneity in adult performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration of spontaneous creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is described as 'a fascinating exploration of the nature of spontaneous creativity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion for both content and outcome: the material should probe how spontaneous creativity operates and provide methods to evoke it in performers.
